title: Config
description:
Per-project factory configuration, i.e. the parsed contents of a
`factory.yaml` file.

$schema.description:
JSON Schema reference for editor completion, e.g.
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stablekernel-blue/sf-factory/main/schema/factory.schema.json`.

Purely advisory: sf-factory does not read this field, editors do.

version.description:
Schema version of this file. Currently always `1`
(`CURRENT_VERSION`). Enforced by the JSON Schema (`sf-factory
validate`) and by editors reading it; not rejected at `serde` parse
time. Migrations to a future version 2 are unplanned and would need
their own design.

name.description:
Human-readable name for this factory, e.g. `"sf-factory"`. Used in
generated resource names and status reporting.

repos.description:
Repositories this factory works on. Must list at least one. Most
factories list exactly one; multi-repo factories are for coordinated
cross-repo work (orchestration and limits apply to the factory as a
whole, not per repo; per-repo orchestration is not yet modeled).

skills.description: Skills available to the factory's agents, beyond OpenCode's built-ins.

commands.description:
Additional OpenCode commands (slash commands) available to the
factory, as paths to markdown command files relative to the repo
root.

orchestration.description: How the factory's agents are organized and looped.

limits.description: Resource and cost limits enforced on the factory's worker.

backend.description: The cloud backend used to launch the factory's worker.

auth.description: How the factory authenticates to the repos and services it uses.

tracker.description:
The issue/work tracker the factory's orchestration loop reads from
and writes to. Defaults to GitHub Issues.

Repo.description: A single repository a factory works on.

base_branch.description:
The base branch the factory opens pull requests against. Defaults to
the repository's default branch when omitted.

Skills.description: Skills available to a factory's agents.

default.description:
Names of shared skills to enable from `stablekernel/skills` (see
[ADR-0006](https://github.com/stablekernel-blue/sf-factory/blob/main/docs/adr/0006-shared-skills-repo.md)),
e.g. `["customize-opencode"]`. An empty list (the default, when
`skills` is omitted entirely) means *no* shared skills are enabled;
there is no way yet to opt into "all shared skills" short of naming
them explicitly. Revisit if that becomes common.

repo.description:
Paths to skill directories inside the factory's own repo(s),
relative to the repo root.

urls.description:
Reserved, not yet implemented (see
[ADR-0006](https://github.com/stablekernel-blue/sf-factory/blob/main/docs/adr/0006-shared-skills-repo.md),
which fetches shared skills via a git checkout of
`stablekernel/skills` and `skills.paths` instead): URLs to
additional skill bundles to fetch at startup.

Orchestration.description: How a factory's agents are organized and how the work loop runs.

roles.description:
Named agent roles available in this factory, keyed by role name
(e.g. `"factory"`, `"reviewer"`).

loop.description:
Configuration for the recurring work loop (audit, assess, execute,
re-evaluate).

A `loop` block with no `strategy` field defaults to the `serial`
strategy, so `factory.yaml` files written before `strategy` existed
keep working unchanged.

Role.description:
A single named agent role in a factory's orchestration.

Per-role handoffs (which role hands work to which) and permission
overrides are left to a follow-up (issue #54). When that lands, a
per-project override may only **tighten**
[`crate::opencode::render`]'s hardened default `permission` block
(see that function's doc comment) — e.g. adding a `deny` rule, or
narrowing an existing `allow` — never loosen it (turning an existing
`deny` into `allow`, or dropping a denylisted pattern entirely).

agent.description:
Name of the OpenCode agent config to use for this role, e.g.
`"factory"`, `"reviewer"`. Corresponds to an agent defined under
`.opencode/agents/`.

model.description:
Model override for this role, named as Bifrost sees it
(`<vendor>/<model>`), e.g. `"anthropic/claude-sonnet-5"`. `None`
uses the agent's own default model. `sf-factory config env` adds
the `bifrost/` provider prefix OpenCode expects
(`"bifrost/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5"`) when setting
`FACTORY_MODEL`, unless the prefix is already present.

LoopConfig.description:
Configuration for the factory's recurring work loop.

How parallel a factory runs is project-specific, so this is keyed by a
`strategy` field: each strategy has its own required fields, and extra
fields that belong to the other strategy (e.g. `concurrency` on a
`serial` loop) are rejected.

A `loop` block with no `strategy` field defaults to `serial`, so
`factory.yaml` files written before `strategy` existed keep parsing
unchanged.

oneOf.description:
One OpenCode session runs `command` repeatedly, working through
ready issues and open PRs one at a time in the same clone. The
default strategy.

command.description:
The OpenCode command that runs one pass of the loop, e.g.
`"factory-loop"`.

max_issues.description: Maximum number of new issues to start per loop pass.

interval_minutes.description:
Minutes to wait between automatic loop passes. `None` means the
loop only runs when triggered manually (e.g. via
`scripts/factory-local loop`).

oneOf.description:
A shell dispatcher claims ready issues and PRs with new feedback and
runs each in its own OpenCode worker and git worktree, up to
`concurrency` at once, polling GitHub every `poll_seconds`.

Every field has a default matching `factory/dispatch.sh`'s own
(env-var) default, so a minimal `strategy: dispatcher` with no other
fields is a valid config (issue #95).

concurrency.description:
Maximum number of concurrent workers. Must be at least 1.
Defaults to `1`, matching `FACTORY_CONCURRENCY`'s default.

issue_command.description:
The OpenCode command a worker runs to implement one claimed
issue and open its PR, e.g. `"factory-issue"`. Defaults to
`"factory-issue"`.

pr_command.description:
The OpenCode command a worker runs to address feedback and
failing checks on one open factory PR, e.g. `"factory-pr"`.
Defaults to `"factory-pr"`.

poll_seconds.description:
Seconds to wait between polls when idle or all worker slots are
full. Must be at least 10, to avoid hammering the tracker's API.
Defaults to `60`, matching `FACTORY_POLL_SECONDS`'s default.

max_issues.description:
Optional cap on new issues started per dispatcher lifetime.
`None` means no cap.

Optional here (unlike `Serial::max_issues`, which is required)
because a dispatcher run is typically long-lived and open-ended
(it keeps polling until stopped), while a serial loop pass is a
single bounded step where a cap is the norm; this matches
`factory/dispatch.sh`'s `FACTORY_MAX_ISSUES`, which is also
optional and empty by default.

exit_when_idle.description:
Whether the dispatcher exits once nothing is running or
dispatchable, instead of polling forever. Defaults to `false`,
matching `FACTORY_EXIT_WHEN_IDLE`'s default.

Limits.description: Resource and cost limits enforced on a factory's worker.

ttl_minutes.description:
Maximum lifetime of the worker in minutes, regardless of activity.
`None` means no hard cap.

idle_minutes.description:
Minutes of inactivity before the worker shuts itself down. `None`
means no idle shutdown.

budget_usd.description:
Maximum gateway spend in US dollars for the worker's lifetime.
`None` means no budget cap is enforced by sf-factory (the gateway
may still enforce its own limits).

memory_mib.description: Memory in MiB allocated to the worker.

spot.description: Whether the worker may run on spot/preemptible capacity.

Backend.description: The cloud backend used to launch a factory's worker.

oneOf.description: Run the worker as an AWS Fargate task.

region.description: AWS region to launch the worker in, e.g. `"us-east-1"`.

oneOf.description: Run the worker as a local Docker container (`scripts/factory-local`).

Auth.description:
How a factory authenticates to the repositories and services it uses.

Both variants hold a *reference* to a secret (`SecretRef`), never a
secret value: `factory.yaml` is checked into source control.

oneOf.description:
A GitHub personal access token scoped to the factory's repos
(Contents, Issues, Pull requests: read/write).

token.description: Reference to the secret containing the token.

oneOf.description:
GitHub App installation auth (issue #45): the backend mints and
refreshes installation tokens itself, so `factory.yaml` only needs
the App and installation identifiers plus a reference to the App's
private key.

installation_id.description: The ID of the App's installation on the factory's repos.

private_key.description: Reference to the secret containing the App's private key (PEM).

SecretRef.description:
A reference to a secret value, never the value itself.

Exactly one of `env` or `secret` must be set; this is enforced by
`serde`'s untagged-enum matching (each variant has a distinct single
field) and by the generated schema (`anyOf`, each branch
`additionalProperties: false`).

anyOf.description:
Read the secret from an environment variable already present in the
worker's environment, e.g. set by the backend from a cloud secret
store.

env.description: Name of the environment variable, e.g. `"GH_TOKEN"`.

anyOf.description:
Resolve the secret from the backend's secret store, e.g. an AWS
Secrets Manager secret name or ARN.

Tracker.description:
The issue/work tracker a factory's orchestration loop reads from and
writes to.

oneOf.description: GitHub Issues on the factory's repo(s). The default.
